page: Amazon Web Services g5g.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by custom AWS Graviton2 processors paired with NVIDIA graphics hardware. The virtual machine provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core). Graphics and machine learning acceleration are driven by a single NVIDIA T4G GPU equipped with 16 GB of video RAM. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks bundled local storage, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal modest general-purpose compute characteristics alongside entry-level GPU processing capability. In CPU stress tests, the 4-core Graviton2 setup registers middle-tier results with 1519.58 in stress-ng single-core and 6054.45 in multi-core metrics. Conversely, Geekbench and PassMark suites highlight weaker instruction and memory pipeline throughput, including a PassMark CPU score of 2697.2 and a memory score of 1044.49. Cryptographic and compression suites also place lower in comparative brackets, while PassMark database operations hold in the median range with 2623.97 points.

On targeted acceleration tasks, the bundled NVIDIA T4G GPU achieves 113.08 tokens per second during prompt ingestion and 49.02 tokens per second for text generation when running small 135M-parameter language models. Memory architecture limits, combined with the lack of local NVMe storage and entry-level 1 Gbps network throughput, mean the instance faces clear bottlenecks when processing heavy datasets or large models.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the pairing of energy-efficient ARM cores with an entry-tier 16 GB accelerator provides a balanced, low-overhead resource profile. AWS g5g.xlarge functions effectively for Android game streaming, lightweight computer vision inference, small-scale graphics rendering, media encoding, and cost-conscious edge or ML microservice deployments requiring ARM and CUDA compatibility.
description: Amazon Web Services g5g.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered with the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. It features 4 dedicated AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, 8.0 GB of system RAM, and a single NVIDIA T4G GPU delivering 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance includes 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and relies entirely on external EBS volumes due to the absence of integrated local storage. Benchmark figures demonstrate average raw multi-core integer performance alongside lower throughput in memory-bound tests and Geekbench workloads. Small model language inference achieves 49.02 tokens per second in text generation. The pairing of low-overhead Graviton cores with entry-level NVIDIA acceleration makes this server suitable for Android application virtualization, edge computer vision inference, lightweight ML serving, and graphics rendering workloads.
